👹🔺️🇺🇸 HUMAN BRAIN POWERED DATA CENTERS 🧠 

Have They Gone Too Far With This One❓️👀

Integrating living brain cells into computer chips creates a hybrid system known as biocomputing or wetware computing. Scientists grow human neurons from adult skin or blood samples reprogrammed into stem cells, then place them onto silicon microchips. 

How It Works:

Electrode Interface: The chip uses microelectrodes to send electrical impulses to the neurons and read their electrical activity.

Life Support: A built-in perfusion circuit acts like a heart and kidneys, pumping a nutrient-rich broth, regulating temperature, mixing gases, and filtering waste to keep the cells alive for months.

Learning: Through electrical feedback loops, the living cells adapt and learn from inputs (such as playing video games like Pong or Doom).

Major Projects & Devices

Cortical Labs (CL1): Melbourne-based Cortical Labs launched the CL1, the world's first commercially available, code-deployable biological computer powered by roughly 200,000 living human neurons.

Brainoware: Researchers at Indiana University Bloomington linked brain organoids (mini-brains) to AI hardware, demonstrating tasks like basic speech recognition.

FinalSpark: A Swiss biocomputing initiative exploring multi-organoid systems hooked up to standard computers via electrodes.

What They Say Key Advantages Are

Extreme Energy Efficiency: While a large AI data center or GPU can consume thousands of watts, a biological neural network operates on just a few watts mimicking the human brain's 20-watt efficiency.

Adaptive Learning: Unlike rigid silicon code, biological neurons naturally reconfigure their connections (synaptic plasticity) to process changing, real-world data with minimal training sets. 

Primary Applications: Rather than replacing traditional computers, these systems are designed for disease modeling, drug discovery, personalized medicine, and testing neurodegenerative treatments without animal testing.
